brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.evidence: The kit has no clock face, dial, hour markers or clock movement. The build is a 7-base hex frame with 6 joint bolts, 2 rod sockets, 1 spool axle and 1 filament spool. It passes check_build (meshClash clear, no loose bodies, no prop warnings) but is not a clock.

Rod sockets accessory:0#-1,0#0 and accessory:0#1,0#3 carry the spool axle axle:0#-1,0#0 across the empty centre cell (0,0). A filament spool hangs on it, so it can rotate on the axle. This is a spool standing in for a hand, not a purpose-made clock hand. Rotation was checked only for placement, not motion.
No hour or minute hand, and no dial markings, exist in the kit. A turning spool cannot show a time. To clear the spool, the neighbouring bases at (0,-1) and (0,1) were removed.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
